author: Hiebl, Schachner, et al.

steps.title: Subculture Caco-2 cells
steps.instruction: Passage Caco-2 cells in 75 cm² flasks using trypsin/EDTA, count, and reseed at defined densities.

substeps.instruction: Pre‑warm PBS, complete growth medium, and trypsin/EDTA for 30 min in a 37 °C water bath.
Discard old medium.
Rinse cells with 12 ml PBS and discard the rinse (volumes refer to 75 cm² flasks).
Add 3 ml trypsin/EDTA, incubate 5 min at 37 °C.
Tap flask sides to detach cells, then add 7 ml complete growth medium to neutralise trypsin.
Gently pipette up‑and‑down to obtain a single‑cell suspension.
Remove 1 ml for cell counting and viability assessment.

Transfer 1 × 10⁶ cells on Monday or 0.5 × 10⁶ cells on Thursday to a new 75 cm² flask and add complete growth medium to a total volume of 15 ml (enables subculturing twice per week; medium renewed every other day, three times per week).
Use cells only between passage numbers 5 and 20.

steps.title: Seed Caco-2 cells on filter inserts
steps.instruction: Prepare and seed Caco-2 cells onto 12‑well translucent inserts for spontaneous differentiation.

substeps.instruction: Pre‑warm PBS, complete growth medium, and trypsin/EDTA for 30 min at 37 °C.
Discard old medium.
Rinse cells with 12 ml PBS and discard.
Add 3 ml trypsin/EDTA, incubate 5 min at 37 °C.
Tap flask sides, add 7 ml complete growth medium to neutralise.
Gently pipette to obtain a single‑cell suspension.
Remove 1 ml for counting and viability.
Pre‑wet each insert (apical side 0.5 ml, basolateral well 1.6 ml) with complete growth medium for ≥2 min.
Reserve one insert without cells for TEER blank measurement (see Supplementary Protocol #3).
Prepare cell suspension at 0.06 × 10⁶ cells / cm²; add 0.5 ml of this suspension to each insert.
Aspirate medium from inserts to be seeded.
Add the cell suspension to each insert and gently shake the plate to distribute cells evenly.
Place plate in a 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ incubator.
After 3 h, replace medium with basolateral medium (both insert and well).
Next day, change medium again to avoid multilayer formation.
Thereafter, change medium every other day (three times per week) for 19–21 days total culture.
Maintain symmetric conditions (basolateral medium in both compartments) for the first 7 days.
On day 7, switch to asymmetric conditions: apical medium serum‑free, basolateral medium containing 20 % FBS.

steps.title: Luciferase reporter assay – cell preparation
steps.instruction: Prepare Caco-2 cells for transfection in 96‑well plates.

substeps.instruction: Pre‑warm PBS, complete growth medium, and trypsin/EDTA for 30 min at 37 °C.
Discard old medium.
Rinse cells with 12 ml PBS and discard.
Add 3 ml trypsin/EDTA, incubate 5 min at 37 °C.
Tap flask sides, add 7 ml complete growth medium to neutralise.
Spin cells at 1400 rpm for 4 min at room temperature.
Resuspend pellet in 10 ml DMEM complete medium by gentle pipetting.
Remove 1 ml for counting and viability.
Plate 0.02 × 10⁶ cells per well (100 µl DMEM complete) in a 96‑well plate; aim for 40–60 % confluence at transfection.
Incubate overnight at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Luciferase reporter assay – transfection
steps.instruction: Transfect Caco-2 cells with expression, reporter, and EGFP plasmids using Lipofectamine™ LTX.

substeps.instruction: 30–60 min before transfection, aspirate medium and add 100 µl OptiMEM reduced‑serum per well.
Prepare DNA/PLUS mixture in OptiMEM (total DNA 0.1 µg per well; PLUS reagent 0.1 µl per well).
Separately dilute Lipofectamine™ LTX (0.5 µl per well) in OptiMEM.
Combine the DNA/PLUS solution with the Lipofectamine™ LTX solution (1:1 volume ratio) as per manufacturer’s instructions.
Mix by pipetting up‑and‑down several times.
Incubate 5 min at room temperature.
Add 10 µl of the DNA/Lipofectamine mixture to each well, gently shake the plate to distribute.
Incubate 24 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Luciferase assay – compound treatment
steps.instruction: Treat transfected cells with test compounds or vehicle.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 2‑fold serial dilutions of compounds in DMEM containing 5 % charcoal‑stripped FBS just before use.
Aspirate old medium, add 50 µl DMEM + 5 % charcoal‑stripped FBS to each well, then add 50 µl compound dilution (final volume 100 µl per well, final compound concentration = 1×).
Incubate 24 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Luciferase assay – cell lysis and measurement
steps.instruction: Lyse cells, measure EGFP fluorescence and luciferase luminescence.

substeps.instruction: Prepare lysis buffer: 4.8 ml H₂O, 1.2 ml 5× lysis buffer, 6 µl CoA (270 mM), 6 µl DTT (1 M).
Aspirate medium, add 50 µl lysis buffer per well, freeze at –80 °C for ≥1 h (up to 1 week) to enhance lysis.
Thaw plate (~30 min), shake 5 min.
Transfer 40 µl lysate to a black 96‑well plate, shake 1 min to remove bubbles.
Measure EGFP fluorescence (excitation 485 nm, emission 520 nm).
Inject 50 µl ATP and 50 µl luciferin, then measure luminescence.
Normalize luciferase luminescence to EGFP fluorescence for each well.

steps.title: Cholesterol uptake assay – micelle preparation
steps.instruction: Prepare 2‑fold concentrated post‑prandial micelles for uptake experiments.

substeps.instruction: Make stock solutions (except sodium taurocholate) in chloroform:methanol 2:1 (v/v); sodium taurocholate stock in serum‑free DMEM.
Pipette required amounts of each stock into a sterile glass vial (except sodium taurocholate).
Add radioactive cholesterol to achieve 1 µCi ml⁻¹ (37 kBq ml⁻¹) final activity.
Evaporate solvent to dryness under gentle nitrogen stream.
Add sodium taurocholate stock solution and serum‑free DMEM to reach desired final volume for 2‑fold micelle concentration.
Vortex 5 min, then incubate 1 h at 37 °C on an orbital shaker (100 rpm).
Prepare treatment medium (DMEM + 1 % human plasma) for basolateral side.
Filter‑sterilise micellar suspension through a 0.45 µm cellulose acetate filter.

steps.title: Cholesterol uptake assay – cell incubation
steps.instruction: Expose differentiated Caco-2 monolayers on inserts to micelles and test compounds.

substeps.instruction: Day 1 (pre‑lunch): Pre‑warm PBS, serum‑free DMEM, and DMEM + 0.5 % BSA at 37 °C.
Aspirate medium from wells and inserts, wash both once with PBS.
Add 0.5 ml serum‑free DMEM to each insert and 1.6 ml DMEM + 0.5 % BSA to each well; incubate 24 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.
Day 2 (pre‑lunch): Pre‑warm PBS and serum‑free DMEM.
Prepare 2‑fold compound dilutions in serum‑free DMEM.
Aspirate medium, wash once with PBS.
Add 0.25 ml serum‑free DMEM to each insert and 1.6 ml serum‑free DMEM to each well.
Add 0.25 ml compound dilution to each insert.
Incubate 48 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.
Day 4 (morning): Add 0.25 ml 2‑fold micelle suspension to each insert and 1.6 ml DMEM + 1 % human plasma to each well.
Add 0.25 ml compound treatment to each insert (treatment lasts 48 h, then micelles + fresh treatment added for another 2 h).
Place plate on orbital shaker (200 rpm) in incubator for 2 h.
Aspirate apical and basolateral media, wash inserts twice with PBS.
Lyse cells with 150 µl NP40 lysis buffer per insert for 30 min at room temperature.
Scratch cells at membrane edge with inoculation needle (avoid tearing).
Transfer lysates to tubes, centrifuge 20 min at 13 000 rpm, 4 °C.
Collect supernatants, add 3.5 ml scintillation fluid to labelled vials, pipet 50 µl lysate and 250 µl micelle control into vials.
Measure dpm with liquid scintillation counter.
Day 5: Perform Bradford assay (or equivalent) on lysates to determine protein concentration for normalisation (dpm / mg protein or nmol / mg protein).

steps.title: Cholesterol efflux assay – cell preparation
steps.instruction: Prepare differentiated Caco-2 monolayers for efflux measurements.

substeps.instruction: Day 1 (morning): Pre‑warm PBS, serum‑free DMEM, and DMEM + 0.5 % BSA at 37 °C.
Aspirate medium from wells and inserts, wash both at least once with PBS.
Add 0.5 ml serum‑free DMEM to each insert and 1.6 ml DMEM + 0.5 % BSA to each well; incubate 24 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Cholesterol efflux assay – micelle and treatment addition
steps.instruction: Apply micelles and test compounds to the apical side of the monolayer.

substeps.instruction: Day 2 (morning): Prepare micelles as in Protocol #4 (without cholesterol) and filter‑sterilise.
Aspirate old medium, wash once with PBS.
Add 1.6 ml serum‑free DMEM to wells and 0.25 ml serum‑free DMEM to inserts.
Add 0.25 ml micelle suspension to each insert; place plate on orbital shaker (200 rpm) at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 24 h.
Day 3 (morning): Pre‑warm PBS and serum‑free DMEM.
Prepare 2‑fold compound dilutions in serum‑free DMEM.
Aspirate medium, wash once with PBS.
Add 0.25 ml serum‑free DMEM to inserts and 1.6 ml serum‑free DMEM to wells.
Add 0.25 ml compound dilution to each insert; incubate 48 h on orbital shaker (200 rpm) at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Cholesterol efflux assay – collection and analysis
steps.instruction: Collect apical/basolateral samples, lyse cells, and quantify cholesterol by scintillation counting.

substeps.instruction: Day 5 (morning): Pre‑warm serum‑free DMEM; prepare DMEM + 1 % human plasma (basolateral acceptor).
Prepare micelles without cholesterol as on Day 2.

Aspirate medium, add 0.25 ml serum‑free DMEM to inserts and 1.6 ml DMEM + 1 % human plasma to wells; add 0.25 ml micelle suspension to inserts; incubate 24 h on orbital shaker (200 rpm) at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.
Day 6 (morning): Collect apical and basolateral supernatants into 2 ml tubes, centrifuge 5 min at 13 000 rpm, 4 °C; transfer supernatants to new tubes.
Wash cells twice with PBS.
If measuring intracellular cholesterol, lyse cells with 150 µl NP40 lysis buffer per insert for 30 min at room temperature, scratch cells with inoculation needle.
Transfer lysates to tubes, centrifuge 20 min at 13 000 rpm, 4 °C; collect supernatants.
Fill scintillation vials with 3.5 ml scintillation fluid, label.
Pipette 50 µl cell lysate, 250 µl apical supernatant, and 800 µl basolateral supernatant into separate vials.
Measure dpm with a liquid scintillation counter.
Perform Bradford assay (or equivalent) on cell lysates to obtain protein concentration; normalise counts to protein (account for differing volumes of apical, basolateral, and lysate samples).

steps.title: Confocal microscopy of cholesterol transporters
steps.instruction: Fix, stain, and image ABCG5, NPC1L1, and ABCB1 in differentiated Caco-2 cells on transparent inserts.

substeps.instruction: Days 1‑2: Follow Supplementary Protocol #5 (identical steps – not reproduced here).
Day 4 (morning): Aspirate medium from wells and inserts, wash twice with PBS.
Fix cells with 3.7 % formaldehyde in PBS for 15 min at room temperature; aspirate formalin and wash twice with PBS.
Permeabilise with 0.2 % Triton X‑100 in PBS for 10 min at room temperature; wash twice with PBS.
Block with 5 % BSA in PBS for 6 h at 4 °C.
Prepare primary‑antibody solutions in PBS + 1 % BSA: ABCG5 2 µg ml⁻¹, NPC1L1 10 µg ml⁻¹ (1:100), ABCB1 2 µg ml⁻¹.
Wash twice with PBS, add 500 µl primary‑antibody solution to each insert, incubate overnight at 4 °C.
Day 5 (morning): Prepare secondary‑antibody solution (Alexa Fluor 488 goat anti‑rabbit, 4 µg ml⁻¹) in PBS + 1 % BSA.
Wash twice with PBS, add 500 µl secondary‑antibody solution to each insert, incubate 3 h at 4 °C in the dark.
Prepare DAPI solution (1 µg ml⁻¹) in PBS + 0.2 % BSA.
Wash twice with PBS, add 500 µl DAPI solution, incubate 15 min at room temperature in the dark.
Wash twice with PBS.

Place one drop of mounting medium on a microscope slide, cut the membrane from the insert with a scalpel, place membrane upside‑down onto the medium, add another drop of medium, cover with a coverslip (avoid bubbles).
Store slides in a dark box at 4 °C until the mounting medium dries; samples are then ready for confocal laser‑scanning microscopy.

steps.title: Resazurin viability and crystal violet staining
steps.instruction: Assess cell viability by resazurin reduction followed by crystal violet staining on differentiated Caco-2 cells on transparent inserts.

substeps.instruction: Days 1‑2: Follow Supplementary Protocol #5 (identical steps – not reproduced here).
Day 4 (morning): Pre‑warm serum‑free DMEM at 37 °C.
Prepare 10 µg ml⁻¹ resazurin solution in serum‑free DMEM.
Aspirate medium from wells and inserts, wash once with serum‑free DMEM.
Add 0.5 ml resazurin solution to each insert and 1.6 ml to each well; incubate 2 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.
Transfer inserts to a new 12‑well plate using forceps.
Collect 400 µl apical medium from each insert into a 48‑well plate and measure fluorescence (excitation 535 nm, emission 590 nm).
Aspirate remaining resazurin solution, add 500 µl crystal violet solution per insert, incubate 10 min at room temperature.
Remove inserts, wash repeatedly with deionised water until wash water is clear (3–5 washes).
Aspirate residual water and let inserts dry overnight at room temperature.
Day 5 (morning): Add 500 µl sodium citrate:ethanol (1:1) to each insert, shake 10 s; add another 500 µl of the same solution, shake 10 s.
Pipette 100 µl from each insert into a 96‑well plate and read absorbance at 595 nm.

steps.title: Statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze experimental data using GraphPad Prism™ 6.01.

substeps.instruction: Perform two‑tailed paired t‑tests for two‑group comparisons.
Conduct one‑way ANOVA with Dunnett post‑test for multiple comparisons; consider p < 0.05 statistically significant.
